summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with embedded firmware experience in C and C++ across ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, Arduino, and NVIDIA Jetson. Wrote bare-metal Cortex-M4 firmware driving GPIO, timers, ADC, and I2C at the register level with interrupt-driven capture and deterministic real-time update rates, and built the Python host-side tooling that links microcontroller firmware to off-target data acquisition.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi over HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; root-caused sensor jitter and resolved it through software calibration and sensor resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a Python tool in PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization, giving lab engineers a host-side interface to instrumented hardware.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor (Cortex-M4)
bullets: Programmed Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal C at the register level (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved a 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM footprint at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver for the display path; verified peripheral timing in Proteus.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN), M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Root-caused 11 hardware and software integration failures across the stack (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) to reach 100% pick reliability over 10 trials at ~11.5 s end-to-end latency.
Wrote the on-controller firmware in C++: two-link inverse kinematics, five-servo actuation, and range-gated contact detection from dual VL53L0X ToF sensors behind a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer.
Linked microcontroller firmware to off-target services over a WebSocket fabric spanning a Flask-SocketIO edge server and an NVIDIA Jetson node.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Streamed YOLOv8 tracking commands from an NVIDIA Jetson to the microcontroller over UART, with interrupt-driven command parsing and a user override path.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control and integrated VL53L0X ToF ranging over I2C with OLED distance readout.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop - Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon - National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
